claim: Heads before appositive of are limited to month and politico-geographical terms.
evidence_summary: The Foreign Office names the Hindu festival of Holi. Holi identifies the festival being celebrated.
finding: Extend the inventory to festival in this identifying use. A festival of music has a different relation.
inference: Must a head in identifying of be month or a politico-geographical term?

evidence.source: UK Foreign & Commonwealth Office (13 March 2017). Alok Sharma extends his wishes for a happy Holi festival.
evidence.passage: §14.3, p. 448, [21]. CGEL restricts heads in the identifying of construction to month and names of politico-geographical categories. The construction specifies which entity bears the name.
evidence.example: The account identifies the occasion celebrated as the Hindu festival of Holi. Compare a festival of music, where music supplies subject matter.
evidence.establishes: Festival admits an identifying use outside CGEL’s stated head inventory.
evidence.locator: Second body paragraph after the photograph, first sentence.
